newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - July 11.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on July 11. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Businessman Aburizal Bakrie, head of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce, said many entrepeneurs were willing to take short cuts using their political connections but this protection would not be available under forthcoming free trade arrangements.

A World Bank executive has told a Jakarta seminar that Indonesia's customs service needs to expedite its new customs clearence system if it did not want to risk being a barrier to sustainable economic growth.

State Secretary Murdiono has said more regional autonomy would be good for Indonesia as an authoritarian government would eventually fall because excessive control created passive and uncreative people.
Discussion between the government and parliament about a law to create a commodity futures market has reached a dead end at the committee stage with neither side giving ground.

A number of private television stations agree with President Suharto's plan to send back the controversial broadcasting bill for re-examination by the parliament as they say it has a number of unclear provisions.
